summary: Anthropic released Claude Opus 5, a new Opus-tier model priced the same as its predecessor Opus 4.8, with detailed benchmark, efficiency and safety disclosures alongside two beta API features.

mechanisms.reason: The document states the new model performs a given task at a lower cost than its predecessor, indicating reduced work per unit of output for equivalent or better quality.
mechanisms.quote: on Frontier-Bench v0.1, Opus 5 surpasses all other models, and more than doubles Opus 4.8’s performance at a lower cost per task.

mechanisms.reason: The lab reports a large, stated jump in performance on a novel-problem-solving benchmark relative to the next-best model.
mechanisms.quote: On ARC-AGI 3 , an evaluation where the model has to solve novel problems, Opus 5’s score is three times as high as the next-best model.

practices.reason: An engineering team choosing a model for coding, reasoning and cost-efficiency has stated benchmark evidence to justify switching to Opus 5.
practices.quote: On coding and knowledge work evaluations like Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA , Opus 5 is the new state-of-the-art

practices.reason: Anthropic describes a purpose-built evaluation for autonomous vulnerability discovery and exploitation, informing how a team could design its own security eval.
practices.quote: This is illustrated by Opus 5’s performance on OSS-Fuzz, an evaluation we’ve developed to assess how well models can find and then exploit vulnerabilities without extensive human guidance.

practices.reason: Teams using the API can now schedule adoption of automatic fallback routing so flagged requests are no longer simply blocked.
practices.quote: Automatic fallbacks on the API. Users can now choose to have requests that are flagged by our safety classifiers on Opus 5 (or Fable 5) automatically route to another model.

practices.reason: The ability to change tools mid-conversation without invalidating the prompt cache lets teams reduce cache-miss cost and latency in agentic sessions.
practices.quote: Mid-conversation tool changes on the Claude Platform. Within a conversation, developers can now change which tools Claude can use without invalidating the prompt cache.

notable_reason: A flagship model release from a leading lab with detailed comparative benchmarks, safety evaluations and new API features warrants attention even though it is not stated to be the top-of-range model.
